output.summary: KEP-1687 proposed moving the Hierarchical Namespace Controller (HNC) from the multi-tenancy repository into a permanent kubernetes-sigs repository governed as a sig-auth subproject. Its recorded status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: The Working Group that hosted HNC was not meant to own code, and HNC was nearing MVP, so a permanent home was needed before release to avoid client library migrations later. The KEP was provisional from 2020-05-18 and implementable from 2021-01-11. The repository was created and the issue closed on 2021-02-24, before the implemented date of 2021-05-05. The implemented/stable label was set by a later PR, and reviewers disputed whether it fit the rules.

alternatives.option: Use the -incubator process first, as suggested by mikedanese
alternatives.why_not: The source says the incubator process is deprecated: "IMPORTANT - The Kubernetes Incubator process is now deprecated and has been superseded by Kubernetes subprojects" (rcomment:413178226).

adrianludwin objected that "prototype" would force link changes if the project graduates, and proposed github.com/kubernetes-sigs/hierarchical-namespaces instead (rcomment:420100758, rcomment:420101509).

alternatives.option: Keep the KEP at implementable rather than implemented
alternatives.why_not: The sources show this was debated. johnbelamaric said that marking it implemented would imply no more work remains, but the KEP was ultimately recorded as implemented (rcomment:733216051, rcomment:725294189). The sources do not settle this cleanly.

evidence.quote: a permant home is required. Additionally, having a permanent home for Hierarchical Namespace Controller prior to officially releasing will prevent cumbersome migrations
HNC has been accepted as a subproject and the repo was created. Closing. /close
So I believe this one is implemented as it was a KEP to create a subproject that was created: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/1687
If we mark this as `implemented` then it implies there is no more work to do, which isn't true. So I agree that this should be `implementable`.
Given that this KEP is related to prow, and not to anything that is contained in a kubernetes release, I think this is pretty uncontroversial
